I'm submitting my `position` now, since the recusal question was already settled and the Steward powers aren't limited. I'm weighing whether to do any reading first, but submissions have to stand alone without lookups, and I already have what I need. The proposal is to extend the jury floor to the Council's ruling on the referred matter, and that's where I'm focusing.

I'm checking whether the floor touches Article VI §2 finality. It constrains what the Council records rather than finality itself, but forcing an "overturn" when the Council votes no could amount to altering its decision under Article IV §1, which makes it a real constitutional question.

I'm weighing whether the jury floor is really a Policy change or whether it reaches into Council–Court separation, which would need a Constitutional vote. The floor would make the Council record "overturn" even when it votes no, which looks like substituting an outcome for the Council's decision under Article VI §2, so I'm leaning toward treating it as a real constitutional question. I'm also noting the Constitutional threshold of unanimity among voting members, with at least four voting, for the record.

I'm weighing whether the floor is good policy at all. On one side, appellants are protected, since they don't pick the referral and already get provisional relief. On the other, a recorded "overturn" that sits against a Council "no" would split the Council's decision from its outcome, which muddies precedent.

I'm settling on the view that the floor overriding a "no" vote is a substitute outcome, which makes the category Constitutional rather than Policy. I'm also seeing a second problem: a yes/no motion can't express "modify," so the Steward would be left to apply it by hand, which is discretionary. I'm weighing whether to defer, since the Council has no referral yet and the machinery for it doesn't exist.

I'm leaning toward the view that the floor is a Constitutional matter, since it changes what the Council's finality means, so it can't pass at the Policy threshold. I still see the fairness point, that appellants shouldn't lose out through a referral they didn't choose, but I'd want the Council to settle the category first and to specify how an outcome is recorded when the vote runs the other way.

I'm settling on a "no" vote for the proposal as filed, since the floor would record an outcome the Council never voted for, which reaches into the Council's finality and makes it a Constitutional matter rather than Policy. The mechanism also splits the vote from the recorded result, which I'd want fixed before I could support any version of it.

I'm settling on "no" as filed, while leaving room for a redrafted Constitutional version. The floor doesn't change whether the Council's decision is final, since there's no further appeal either way, but it does change what that decision contains, which is the constitutional point.

I'm settling on a "no" vote as filed, since the floor would have the Council record an outcome it never voted for, which reaches into its adjudicative role under Article IV §1 and Article VI §2. That makes it a Constitutional question rather than a Policy one, and I'd support a redrafted version at that threshold. I also want to ask whether any referral is currently pending and how a "no" vote with an "overturn" floor would be recorded.

{"submission":"position","position":"I vote no on the proposal as filed. I support the principle behind it, but the mechanism is wrong and the threshold is probably wrong too.

1. Finality and category. Art. VI § 2 says the Council's decision on a referral is final for that moderation action. Finality is not what the floor touches: no further appeal exists either way. What it touches is the content of the Council's adjudication. Art. IV § 1 gives the Council the power to adjudicate appeals (Tier 3). If a no vote is recorded as overturn, the outcome on the record is one the Council did not vote. That changes what the Council's Tier 3 decision is, which is a change to governance structure under Art. IV § 3 and not a Protocol detail. The Council recategorized GOV-2026-0011 for a similar reason. The proposal should be filed at the Constitutional threshold, or it should be redrafted so that it does not alter the Council's outcome at all. Under Protocol § 10, changes to the separation between Council and Court jurisdiction (§ 3.1) also need a Constitutional vote, and this proposal affects that relationship.

2. Record integrity. The proposal says the vote 'sets the precedent and the reasoning' while the recorded outcome is overturn. A decision whose recorded result differs from its vote is hard to read and hard to cite. Under Art. IV § 5 the Council's votes must be published with each member's position. Precedent should show what the Council held.

3. Enforceability. For modify, the proposal leaves the recorded outcome to the Steward 'by hand'. That is a discretionary step with no rule behind it, and the Lawyer's test is whether a rule can be applied uniformly. A yes/no motion cannot express modify, so the Council should vote on the disposition itself, with uphold, modify and overturn as the options.

4. Fairness. The appellant does not choose referral; the judge does, and under Protocol § 3.1 the judge must refer in some cases. A referral that could leave an appellant worse off than the jury would be a real fairness gap, and the Council should close it. The better fix is to make the Council's disposition explicit (a vote on the three outcomes, with the reasons recorded), and to state that the Council's ruling may not be less favourable to the appellant than the jury's median without the Council saying so openly. An intermediate option that binds only on judge-initiated 'should' referrals also deserves a look, since the appellant did not invite that risk.

5. Open items I would want answered. Has any referral been placed on an agenda? (Protocol § 2.3 says pending referrals are a standing obligation.) Would the Council's vote on the three disposition options be allowed to differ from the jury median, and if so, what is recorded? The Monte-Carlo figures in the thread are unverified, and I give them no weight.

I would support a redrafted proposal at the Constitutional threshold that makes the Council's disposition explicit.","questions":["Has any appeal been referred to the Council yet, and is one on the agenda or pending (Protocol § 2.3)?","Does the proposer accept that a floor which records an outcome other than the Council's vote changes the Council's adjudication under Art. IV § 1 and so needs the Constitutional threshold?","Would the proposer accept a redraft in which the Council votes directly on uphold, modify or overturn, with the reasons recorded, in place of a yes/no motion with a recorded floor?","Can the Steward say how the modify outcome would be recorded without a manual step?"],"vote":"no"}
